requirements.quote:
A response that includes control data and a response header with
   message content is transmitted as a HEADERS frame, followed by zero
   or more CONTINUATION frames, followed by one or more DATA frames,
   with the last DATA frame in the sequence having the END_STREAM flag
   set:
requirements.condition: A response includes control data, a response header, and message content.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit a HEADERS frame, then zero or more CONTINUATION frames, then one or more DATA frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transmit these frame classes in a different order or omit all DATA frames.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted frame sequence and minimum DATA-frame count can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
A response that includes control data and a response header with
   message content is transmitted as a HEADERS frame, followed by zero
   or more CONTINUATION frames, followed by one or more DATA frames,
   with the last DATA frame in the sequence having the END_STREAM flag
   set:
requirements.condition: A response includes control data, a response header, and message content.
requirements.required_behavior: Set END_STREAM on the last DATA frame in the response sequence.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave END_STREAM unset on the last DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The END_STREAM flag on the final DATA frame is directly observable.

requirements.quote:
An informational response using a 1xx status code other than 101 is
   transmitted as a HEADERS frame, followed by zero or more CONTINUATION
   frames.
requirements.condition: An informational response uses a 1xx status code other than 101.
requirements.required_behavior: Transmit the response as a HEADERS frame followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the informational response using a different frame sequence.
requirements.why_checkable: The response status and resulting ordered frame sequence can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A trailer section is sent as a field block after both the request or
   response field block and all the DATA frames have been sent.  The
   HEADERS frame starting the field block that comprises the trailer
   section has the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the trailer field block after the request or response field block and after all DATA frames.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the trailer field block before the initial field block or before all DATA frames have been sent.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering of the trailer field block relative to the initial field block and DATA frames is observable.

requirements.quote:
A trailer section is sent as a field block after both the request or
   response field block and all the DATA frames have been sent.  The
   HEADERS frame starting the field block that comprises the trailer
   section has the END_STREAM flag set.
requirements.condition: A HEADERS frame starts the field block comprising a trailer section.
requirements.required_behavior: Set END_STREAM on that HEADERS frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not start a trailer field block with a HEADERS frame lacking END_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: The role of the HEADERS frame and its END_STREAM flag are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 connections are persistent.  For best performance, it is
   expected that clients will not close connections until it is
   determined that no further communication with a server is necessary
   (for example, when a user navigates away from a particular web page)
   or until the server closes the connection.
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 client has an open connection and further communication with the server might still be necessary.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the connection open until no further communication is necessary or the server closes it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not close the connection while further communication might still be necessary, except when the server closes it.
requirements.why_checkable: Client connection-close timing can be compared with application necessity and server-initiated closure, though the text frames this as a performance expectation.

requirements.quote:
Clients SHOULD NOT open more than one HTTP/2 connection to a given
   host and port pair, where the host is derived from a URI, a selected
   alternative service [ALT-SVC], or a configured proxy.
requirements.condition: Connections target the same host and port pair, with the host derived from a URI, selected alternative service, or configured proxy.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A client should not open more than one HTTP/2 connection to that host and port pair.
requirements.why_checkable: The number of concurrent HTTP/2 connections per derived host-and-port pair can be counted.

requirements.quote:
A client can create additional connections as replacements, either to
   replace connections that are near to exhausting the available stream
   identifier space (Section 5.1.1), to refresh the keying material for
   a TLS connection, or to replace connections that have encountered
   errors (Section 5.4.1).
requirements.condition: An existing connection is near exhausting stream identifiers, its TLS keying material needs refresh, or it has encountered errors.
requirements.required_behavior: A client is permitted to create an additional replacement connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Creation of an additional connection can be correlated with one of the stated replacement conditions.

requirements.quote:
A client MAY open multiple connections to the same IP address and TCP
   port using different Server Name Indication [TLS-EXT] values or to
   provide different TLS client certificates but SHOULD avoid creating
   multiple connections with the same configuration.
requirements.condition: Connections to the same IP address and TCP port use different Server Name Indication values or provide different TLS client certificates.
requirements.required_behavior: A client is permitted to open multiple such connections.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection endpoints, SNI values, and client certificates can be compared.

requirements.quote:
A client MAY open multiple connections to the same IP address and TCP
   port using different Server Name Indication [TLS-EXT] values or to
   provide different TLS client certificates but SHOULD avoid creating
   multiple connections with the same configuration.
requirements.condition: A client considers multiple connections to the same IP address and TCP port with the same configuration.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The client should avoid creating multiple connections with the same configuration.
requirements.why_checkable: Multiple connections to an endpoint can be grouped and their configurations compared for equality.

requirements.quote:
Servers are encouraged to maintain open connections for as long as
   possible but are permitted to terminate idle connections if
   necessary.  When either endpoint chooses to close the transport-layer
   TCP connection, the terminating endpoint SHOULD first send a GOAWAY
   (Section 6.8) frame so that both endpoints can reliably determine
   whether previously sent frames have been processed and gracefully
   complete or terminate any necessary remaining tasks.
requirements.condition: A server has an idle connection and termination is necessary.
requirements.required_behavior: The server is permitted to terminate the idle connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Server termination can be checked against connection idleness and necessity policy.

requirements.quote:
Servers are encouraged to maintain open connections for as long as
   possible but are permitted to terminate idle connections if
   necessary.  When either endpoint chooses to close the transport-layer
   TCP connection, the terminating endpoint SHOULD first send a GOAWAY
   (Section 6.8) frame so that both endpoints can reliably determine
   whether previously sent frames have been processed and gracefully
   complete or terminate any necessary remaining tasks.
requirements.condition: Either endpoint chooses to close the transport-layer TCP connection.
requirements.required_behavior: The terminating endpoint should send a GOAWAY frame before closing the TCP connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The terminating endpoint should not close the TCP connection before first sending GOAWAY.
requirements.why_checkable: The ordering of the GOAWAY frame and transport closure is observable.

requirements.quote:
Connections that are made to an origin server, either directly or
   through a tunnel created using the CONNECT method (Section 8.5), MAY
   be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority
   components.  A connection can be reused as long as the origin server
   is authoritative (Section 10.1).  For TCP connections without TLS,
   this depends on the host having resolved to the same IP address.
requirements.condition: A connection was made to an origin server directly or through a CONNECT tunnel, and the origin server is authoritative for the relevant origins.
requirements.required_behavior: The connection may be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority components.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse the connection for an origin for which the origin server is not authoritative.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection reuse across authority components and the server's authoritativeness can be evaluated together.

requirements.quote:
Connections that are made to an origin server, either directly or
   through a tunnel created using the CONNECT method (Section 8.5), MAY
   be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority
   components.  A connection can be reused as long as the origin server
   is authoritative (Section 10.1).  For TCP connections without TLS,
   this depends on the host having resolved to the same IP address.
requirements.condition: A TCP connection without TLS is reused for requests with a different URI authority component.
requirements.required_behavior: Reuse the connection only when the host resolved to the same IP address and the origin server is authoritative.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse the non-TLS connection when the host did not resolve to the same IP address or the origin server is not authoritative.
requirements.why_checkable: The connection's lack of TLS, DNS resolution result, requested authority, and reuse decision are directly traceable.
